                                           PERSONAL INFORMATION:

 1   Q. Please state your name and address.

 2   A. My name is Mark Allan Bradbury. My address is 504 Grand Ave, Brady, TX 76825.


 3   Q. Are you the same Mark AIIan Bradbury who filed a Motion to Intervene in this

 4   proceeding?

 5   A. Yes. PUC Docket Number 59475,1027. Motion to Intervene


 6   Q. Please state your background.


7    A. I am a property owner and Ieaser of property that is impacted by multiple portions of the

 8   transmission line and seek full party status under 16 TAC §22.103(a) as a person whose legal

 9   rights, duties, or privileges will be directly affected.

10   Q. Are you testifying on behalf of the above-listed Iandowner?


11   A. Yes


12   Q. Is the property affected by the transmission line project proposed by Oncor Electric

13   Delivery Company LLC?


14   A. Yes

15   Q. What is the purpose of yourtestimony?


16   A. Movant protests the application on the following grounds:

17       1. Failure to Meet CCN Requirements


18            The application fails to demonstrate compliance with Texas Utilities Code §37. 056(c),

19            including:

20               •    Inadequate demonstration of need
                                                                    Direct Testimony of Mark Allan Bradbury
                                                                                    PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                            SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                               Page 4 of 15
                •   Failure to prioritize existing ROW corridors

 2             •   Insufficient consideration of community values


 3      2. Improper Routing Analysis


 4         The proposed route does not represent the least impactful alternative when evaluated

 5         under 16 TAC §25.101(b)(3)

 6      3. Disproportionate Rural Burden


 7         The routing imposes excessive impact on Concho, McCulloch and Menard County

 8         landowners relative to system-wide benefits.

 9      4. Environmental and Agricultural Harm


10         The application fails to adequately assess impacts to:

               •   Ranching operations


12             •   Agritourism and hunting operations

13             •   Soil stability

14             •   Wildlife habitat


15   Q. What are the routes on these properties?


16   A. Route N12-tract 235;


17   Routes N2/N11 - tracts 262, 263, 348, 352, and 355


18   Route M12-tracts 355, 360, 4028,4029, 4402,4403, 678, 4404, 4405, 679,4406, 4407,

19   4408,4409,4410,4411,4412,4413, and 4419.


20   Q. What routes do you oppose?
                                                                  Direct Testimony of Mark Allan Bradbury
                                                                                  PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                          SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                             Page 5 of 15
  1   A. I oppose routes N12, N2/N11 and M12 asthese routesdo notrepresenttheleast impactful

2    alternative when evaluated under 16 TAC §25.101(b)(3)

 3   Q. What routes do you prefer?


4    A. I prefer using existing routes, either the north existing right-of-way or the south existing right-

 5   of-way in Exhibit A, "Existing Transmission Lines in Area". These routes should have been

6    evaluated and selected under 16 TAC §25.101(b)(3) and provide minimal impact to one ofthe

7    last large undisturbed areas in Texas. These routes:


8        1.   Maximize existing corridor co-location

9        2.   Minimize residential proximity

10       3.   Reduce agricultural fragmentation

         4. Avoid environmentally sensitive areas


12   Q. Have you ever testified at the Public Utility Commission of Texas before?


13   A. No

14   Q. Was this material prepared by you or under your supervision?


15   A. Yes, this material was prepared by myself.

                                       DESCRIPTION AND LOCATION

 1   Q. Do you have pictures that depict the property and how it is used?


 2   A. Yes, see Exhibit B, "Pictures of Property".

 3   Q. Have the pictures been altered?


 4   A. A copy of each picture, denoted as altered, shows the approximate scale and location of the

 5   transmission line. These were created by ChatGPT using exact coordinates of picture locations

 6   and proposed route of transmission line.

 7   Q. Do the pictures accurately represent the views of the property?


 8   A. Yes

 9   Q. Description of the properties?


10   A. Large contiguous ranches that consist of native live oak, cedar and mesquite on slightly

11   rolling terrain. Area includes seasonal creeks and draws, with thin topsoil over Iimestone or

12   caliche. Primarily used for cattle grazing, hunting and recreation.

13   Q. Where is your location in the study area?


14   A. On route N12 - tract 235, routes N2/N11 - tracts 262, 263, 348, 352, and 355 and route

15   M12 -tracts 355, 360, 4028, 4029,4402, 4403, 678, 4404,4405, 679, 4406, 4407, 4408,4409,

16   4410,4411,4412,4413, and 4419.


17

                                 LAND USE, CONCERNSAND HISTORY

 1   Q. Please give a brief history of the property and your association with it.


 2   A. My ranch, part ofwhich is tract 235 on route N12, is part ofthe original Loveless ranch and

 3   the location of the official Texas ghost town of Loveless established in the early 1900s. My ranch

 4   still contains the Loveless Cemetery, the original farmhouse and bams, and contains parts of

 5   foundations from some of the original town buildings.

 6   I also lease the land affected by routes N2/N11 - tracts 262, 263, 348, 352, and 355 and route

7    M12 - tracts 355, 360, 4028, 4029, 4402, 4403, 678, 4404, 4405, 679, 4406, 4407, 4408, 4409,

 8   4410,4411,4412,4413, and 4419. This land is part ofthe historic Ford Ranch, one ofthe

 9   largest contiguous cattle and hunting ranches in Central Texas. The Ford Ranch was home to

10   the legendary Brady Buck which held the world record for non-typical whitetail deer for nearly 90

11   years.

12   Q. Please describe how the property is used today and how this transmission line may

13   affect that use.

14   A. My property is used for cattle ranching, hunting and is the future location of my home. The

15   transmission line would limit or preclude building my home and limit the acreage available for

16   ranching and hunting.

17   The property I lease is now owned by Hamlin Cattle Company for cattle ranching and leased by

18   myself, as Heart of Texas Bowhunting, LLC for agritourism and hunting activities. The

19   transmission line would destroy native wildlife habitat used by multiple game varieties and
20   reduce the acreage available for use in my business.




                                                                 Direct Testimony of Mark Allan Bradbury
                                                                                 PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                         SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                            Page 8 of 15
  1   Q. What types of concerns do you have with regard to the transmission line segments

2    and routes proposed?

3    A. The proposed transmission line would have the following impacts on agricultural operations:

4       •   Interfere with grazing patterns


5       •   Restrict equipment movement


6       •   Reduce usable acreage

7       •   Introduce long-term operational inefficiencies


8    Such infrastructure will fragment wildlife habitats, impact native ecosystems, and contribute to

9    soil erosion and water resource disruption.

10

                                                                                  PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                          SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349

                                              FINANCIAL RISKS

 1    Q. What do you think the financial risks will be to you?


 2    A. My property value and therefore the value of my estate will decrease drastically I will also

 3    have a large yearly financial impact based on reduced land on which to run Heart of Texas

 4    Bowhunting, LLC. The proposed routes affect approximately 13 miles of leased and owned

 5    acreage. Atthe minimum 200 foot requiredwidth, this removes approximately 315 acres from

 6    use. This has a direct annual negative effect of $49,000 per year at current pricing to my

 7    bowhunting operation.

 8    Q. What are the risks of devaluation of your property?


 9    A. This is not a risk; it is a given. Large transmission lines and other easements devalue

'\O   property. Attached as Exhibit C, "Affidavit of Property Value Impact", is a statement from a

11    licensed agent in our area that specializes in farm and ranch properties.

12

                                                                                   PUC Docket No. 59475

                              HEALTH RISKS, ENVIRONMENTAL AND WILDLIFE


 1   Q. What do you think are the health risks?


 2   A. High-voltage transmission lines generate electromagnetic fields (EMFs) and other

 3   emanations, and while research is ongoing, there are concerns about potential long-term

 4   exposure effects, particularly for families living in close proximity to these corridors.

 5   Q. What do you see as safety risks?


 6   A. Texas and this region is known for its devastating tornadoes and thunderstorms. These

 7   massive structures and high power levels could cause fire and other safety issues if damaged

 8   by a severe storm, hit by lightning or brought down by a tornado.

 9   Q. What do you think will be the environmental impacts and risks?


10   A. the environmental consequences of a 765 kV transmission corridor are considerable. Such

11   infrastructure can fragment wildlife habitats, impact native ecosystems, and contribute to soil
12   erosion and water resource disruption. These impacts are especially concerning in sensitive and

13   agriculturally productive regions of Texas.

14   Q. What do you think will be the risks to birds and native wildlife?


15   A. Concho, McCulloch and Menard counties are located in the transition zone between the

16   Edwards Plateau and the Rolling Plains, and host several rare and noteworthy breeding bird

17   species, particularly along riparian corridors and in shrubby, mesquite habitats. The disruption

18   and fracturing of this habitat will cause declines in nesting and breeding sites . Destruction of
19   native cover and bisection of natural wildlife travel corridors will have a distinct effect on the

20   wildlife in the area.

21   Q. What do you think will be the risks to your agricultural activities and animals?
                                                                     Direct Testimony of Mark Allan Bradbury
                                                                                     PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                             SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                               Pag e 11 of 15
 1   A. This transmission line will have strong impacts on grazing patterns, physical effects on cattle

2   and wildlife, and disruption of agricultural activities.

3   Q. What do you think will be the risks to your stock tanks and ground water?


4   A. Soil erosion, disruption of natural waterways, and other effects from the large, cleared

5   footprint of this easement will muddy stock tanks and change watersheds affecting ground

6   water.

7




                                                                 Direct Testimony of Mark Allan Bradbury
                                                                                 PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                         SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                           Page 12 of 15
                         RECREATION, COMMUNITY VALUES AND AESTHETICS

 1   Q. How would this transmission line affect your enjoyment of your property?


 2   A. The proposed transmission line will destroy the natural beauty and scenic views on our

 3   property. It will limit how we use parts of the property, introduce noise and visual intrusion and

 4   reduce the sense of privacy and the rural character of the property This line would affect some

 5   of the very reasons we bought the property.

 6   Q. Do you think the proposed transmission line will affect any planned future use on your

 7   land?

 8   A. The proposed transmission line will at least limit the location of and most likely will preclude

 9   any future home site on my property. Both the visual disruption and physical effects of EMF and

10   other emanations from these 765 kV lines will require my family to relocate planned building

11   sites or abandon building on the property altogether.

12   Q. How would this transmission line affect your rural community values for your area?


13   A. The scale of 765 kV infrastructure will permanently alter the character of rural communities,

14   affecting scenic landscapes and quality of life.

15   Q. How will this transmission line affect the aesthetic value of your property?


16   A. This line will disrupt the most scenic views on our property and generate noise and other

17   emanations that will greatly detract from the aesthetic value of my property.

18




                                                                    Direct Testimony of Mark Allan Bradbury
                                                                                    PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                            SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                              Page 13 of 15
                              LOCAL ELECTRICITY SERVICE AND COSTS.

1   Q. Do you think that this transmission line will improve your electric service in your

2   area?

3   A. No. This line connects two substations that are multiple counties away from this area and will

4   not provide any service to Concho, McCulloch or Menard counties.

5   Q. Do you think this transmission line will lower your electricity costs?


6   A. No. This line will likely increase electricity costs across the state by forcing taxpayers to fund

7   its construction and the purchase of easements.

8




                                                                   Direct Testimony of Mark Allan Bradbury
                                                                                   PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                           SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                             Page 14 of 15
                                 CONCLUSIONSAND RECOMMENDATION

 1   Q: Is there anything else you would like to have considered in this proceeding?


 2   A. This project is not just infrastructure, it is a permanent industrial corridor across our counties.

 3   Under Texas law, the Public Utility Commission of Texas must consider community values,

 4   environmental integrity, and the use of existing rights-of-way/easements before approving a

 5   transmission line. The evidence demonstrates that the proposed routes do not represent the

 6   least impactful option.

7    The depicted alternative routes are clearly superior under the criteria set forth in Texas Utilities

 8   Code §37.056 and 16 TAC §25.101 because they reduce residential, agricultural, and

 9   environmental impacts while maximizing use of existing corridors.

10   Additionally, Texas currently has a power generation shortfall, with tighter margins due to high

11   demand growth. Where is the power to supply these proposed lines coming from? Will this

12   transfer of power across the state cause further requirements for conservation during times of

13   peak load? As one of the most energy rich areas of the state, why not use the abundant natural

14   resources in west Texas to generate power locally?


15   I respectfullyrequestthatthe Commission reject the proposedroutesthrough Concho,

16   McCulloch and Menard Counties and require adoption or further evaluation of alternative routes.

17   Q. Does the conclude your testimony?


18   A. Yes
